expect.note: EXPECT REWRITTEN — the recorded expect (chosen=null, identity_confirmed NOT true) is REFUTED on measurement, and its proposed mechanism is refuted empirically. (1) It demands a refusal on a bioconda-anchored EXACT-name match — the brief's named anti-pattern (39 names, 0 wrong; keep the short-circuit). bioconda 'atlas' IS a real bio tool at the exact name asked for; 'metagenome-atlas' is a DIFFERENT name the user could have typed. (2) Its mechanism — 'when sibling bioconda packages share the name as substring/acronym, demand the user pick' — I ran it: bwa has 14 bioconda siblings (bwa-mem2, bwakit, bwameth, ...), muscle 2, busco 4, hmmer 3. The rule REFUSES bwa/muscle/busco/hmmer — 4 of 9 canonical tools tested, the exact false-accusation the brief forbids. (3) identity_confirmed=false is also unbuildable: I measured domain_signal() on the bioconda summaries of all 10 named canonical tools — bwa/fastqc/hmmer/macs2/prokka/muscle/iqtree/busco/bracken/humann ALL return [] — so any description-reading confirmation rule marks 10/10 unconfirmed. THE REAL, BUILDABLE DEFECT IS THE REPORT, hence gap_class report: identity.note=='' silences all doubt while identity.self_description holds the evidence one field away. Fix = keep the pick and confirmed=true (bioconda genuinely anchors DOMAIN), and ALWAYS populate note with the self_description on the bioconda branch — a uniform DISCLOSURE ('bioconda anchors domain, not identity; this package says: X — confirm'), which accuses nobody and matches resolver.py's own stated philosophy ('does not gate ... puts the package's OWN self-description in front of whoever decides'). ASSERT: chosen=='conda' AND identity.confirmed is True — a REGRESSION GUARD protecting the pick from a well-meaning refuse-fix. SCHEMA GAP, stated plainly: the decisive assertion (identity.note != '') has no field in this schema, so a pytest built from this row PASSES today and does NOT prove the report fix. Add a note_nonempty field. AMBIGUOUS NULLED (was true): live, it fires on a THIRD and FOURTH unrelated atlas (PyPI = AI-agent environments, CRAN = a Stanford search API) — a pure third-party accident that says nothing about the ancient-DNA/metagenome collision.
